"# Corpus fixtures for sweep-retros counter tests\n\n## WHY THESE EXIST — AND WHY THEY MUST NOT BE REWRITTEN\n\nThese fixtures are FROZEN COPIES of shape-bearing lines from the real retro\ncorpus, NOT hand-written exercises in what the counter \"should\" count.\n\nThe distinction is the entire point. The delta counter in sweep-retros.sh\nwas broken TWICE before commit 1a2f738. Both failures had the same cause:\nthe fixtures agreed with the wrong assumption — they were written from\nretro.template.md, not from retros the corpus actually produced. The counter\npassed every synthetic test and silently miscounted every real retro it\ntouched.\n\nThe third repair anchored cases 38-45 to eight real files on disk and\ndiscovered the failure modes the earlier fixtures had hidden (P-prefix\nheadings, bare-number headings). This directory replaces the live-file\ndependency so those same cases run on any machine.\n\n## What \"frozen\" means here\n\nEach fixture preserves:\n- The LEADING MARKER BLOCK verbatim — `<!-- review-status: ... -->` and any\n  companion metadata comments, in the exact form and order they appear in\n  the real file.\n- Every count-bearing heading verbatim — structural prefix (`## P1`, `## D13`,\n  `## 1.`) and title text, in the exact order they appear in the original.\n  Where a heading title contains a client-identifying string (target hostname,\n  site name), ONLY THAT TITLE TEXT is replaced with a neutral placeholder;\n  the structural prefix is never touched.\n- Table row SHAPES verbatim — for retros that list deltas as `| N | … |` rows,\n  every row is present in original order with its first cell untouched. The\n  counter reads only that first cell, so the remaining columns carry no\n  information the regression needs.\n\nBody prose between headings is omitted — the counter ignores it.\n\n## What was redacted and why\n\nThese retros were produced by real research runs, several of them on an active\nclient engagement. Everything a fixture does NOT need is stripped, because a\nfixture that carries content it does not need is a leak waiting for someone to\ncopy it somewhere else.\n\nRedacted, in every occurrence:\n\n- engagement identifiers (focus names, target hostnames, site names) in heading\n  titles and in `<!-- target: … -->` leading-block comments, replaced with\n  `target-01` / `target-02` / `focus-a` / `focus-b` / `focus-c` / `focus-d`;\n- ALL table-row prose beyond the first cell. This is the one that bit us: the\n  first version of these fixtures kept table rows whole, and the evidence column\n  turned out to carry decompiled symbol names, proprietary binary names and\n  commit hashes from the client's own repository. A review caught it before it\n  shipped. The counter never reads past the first cell, so none of it was\n  needed.\n\nNo heading PREFIX and no first table cell was changed, so no count moved.\n\nThe rule this leaves behind: redact everything the counter does not read. If you\nare unsure whether a fixture needs some text, it does not.\n\n## The regression lives in the shapes\n\nReplacing these fixtures with hand-written heredocs restores the historical\nfailure mode: if you write headings that look like what you EXPECT the corpus\nto produce, you will miss the forms the corpus ACTUALLY produces. The counter\nmissed P-prefix headings (P1, P2 …) for exactly this reason. It missed\nbare-number headings (## 1., ## 2. …) for the same reason.\n\nIf a NEW heading form appears in a real retro that the counter does not yet\nrecognise, the right action is:\n1. Add a frozen sample of that retro to this directory. Name the file after the\n   shape it demonstrates (e.g. `p-prefix-headings-N.md`), not the engagement.\n2. Redact the sample: strip all body prose; replace every engagement identifier\n   (focus names, target hostnames, site names) in heading titles and leading-block\n   metadata with neutral placeholders (`target-01`, `focus-a`, `focus-b`, …);\n   blank every table-row cell beyond the first. Keep every count-bearing element\n   (structural heading prefix, first table cell) byte-identical. Keeping the shape\n   real while keeping the content minimal are BOTH required — whichever one is\n   absent is the one that gets skipped.\n3. Add a test case pinning its expected count.\n4. Fix the counter until the test passes.\n\nDo NOT add a synthetic fixture for the new form and call it done — that is\nhow the counter was broken twice before.\n\n## The synthetic exception\n\nCase 46 in sweep-retros.test.sh tests spaceless em-dash and en-dash\nseparators (`## P1—title`, `## D2–title`). This shape does NOT exist in the\nreal corpus today; the synthetic fixture is deliberately labelled as such so\nit is not mistaken for a frozen corpus sample. When a real retro does use\nthis separator form, add a frozen fixture here and retire the synthetic case.\n"

"# Lane fixture layout\n\nFixtures for the fast/slow test-lane system live here, one subdirectory per suite:\n\n```\nfixtures/lane/\n  <suite-name>/\n    <fixture-name>.json\n```\n\nExample: `fixtures/lane/corroborate-ghidra/baseline.json`\n\n## Purpose\n\nIn the **fast** lane (the default gate), suites load these pre-captured JSON\nfixtures instead of spawning the real tool (Ghidra, r2, bwrap, etc.).  This\nkeeps `run-all.sh` under ~30 s on developer machines while still exercising\nevery assertion that does not require a live tool.\n\nContainment guards (bwrap / qemu / docker flags) are asserted in the fast lane\ntoo — only the real-tool spawn is deferred.\n\n## Generating fixtures\n\nRun `regen-lane-fixtures.sh` (in the parent `tests/` directory) to rebuild\nall fixtures from a live slow-lane run.  A real tool installation is required\nfor regeneration; it is NOT required for the fast-lane gate.\n\n## Anti-#128 rule\n\nA fast-lane suite MUST emit a normal `== N passed · N failed ==` summary.\nIt must NEVER emit a `SKIP:` line — `run-all.sh` counts `SKIP:+exit0` as\nskipped (= lost coverage).\n"

"<!-- review-status: pending -->\n# Retro — 2026-09-17 tooling: search core, ranking, semantic, unified 3-source, preview auto-mock, kit lints\n\n**Trigger:** operator hit `corpus-nav find \"No matches\"` on valid multi-word queries; root-caused to a literal-whole-query-substring matcher. Audit found the SAME bug in `niagara_help`. Operator then asked to innovate/improve the tools (chain #1–#7, high→low).\n\n## What shipped (all verified by RUNNING)\n\n| # | Change | Files | Verify |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | **Shared search core** `parse_query / file_matches(and\\|or) / line_hits / score` | `tools/lib/textsearch.py` (+`test_textsearch.py`, 24 tests) | 24/24 pass |\n| 2 | **Self-tests** on the search tools | `corpus-nav.py selftest`, `niagara_help.py selftest` | all assertions pass |\n| 3 | **Relevance ranking + `--and/--or`** | `corpus-nav.py`, `niagara_help_lib/{find,guide}_search.py`, `niagara_help.py` | best-first; single-word unchanged |\n| 4 | **Unified 3-source search** (FUENTE 1 blocks + 2 docs + 3 code), typed unavailable (never silent-zero) | `tools/find3.py` (new) | 3 sources return / typed `[!]` |\n| 5 | **Semantic ranking** (TF-IDF cosine, pure-Python, ~1s/1005 blocks) | `corpus-nav.py semantic\\|rank` | B1015/B736 rank high on concept queries |\n| 6 | **`dashboard-preview --auto-mock`** (mock from the reader's slot arrays) + `--live` proxy | `tools/dashboard-preview.py` | 80-key mock auto-generated for UmbrellaDashboard |\n| 7 | **build-n4 kit lints**: `lint-lexicon-ascii` (new), plano SKIP on 3D SPA, phantom-dep recognizes `project(:X)`, build.sh hints | kit `toolbelt/*`, `tests/*` | 58/58 bats, shellcheck OK, report-module CLEAN |\n\n## Root cause + fix (the class)\nTwo independent tools matched the ENTIRE query as one literal case-insensitive substring (`query in line`), so any non-verbatim multi-word query returned zero. Fixed by tokenizing and matching by TERMS: corpus-nav = OR-any (small corpus, ranked); niagara_help = AND-per-file (huge doc corpus, no flood). Consolidated into ONE `textsearch.py` so it can never drift/re-appear, guarded by self-tests.\n\n## Evidence (before → after)\n- `corpus-nav find \"BStatus overridden\"` 0 → 50 (ranked). `guide-search \"alarm fault\"` 0 → 603. `devguide-search \"servlet override\"` 0 → 8. `find \"setpoint override\"` 19 → 209.\n- `corpus-nav semantic \"point health fault override status\"` → B808/B1017/B736 top (BStatus concept surfaced by IDF weighting).\n\n## Lessons\n- The same search bug lived in TWO tools because search logic was duplicated — a shared core + self-tests is the systemic fix, not per-tool patches.\n- Semantics should match corpus size: OR-ranked for ~1000 small blocks; AND-per-file for thousands of docs; TF-IDF cosine when you want concept-relevance without neural deps.\n- A search tool must return a TYPED unavailable (tool missing/timeout/error) — never fold it into \"no results\", or a negative becomes a false \"does not exist\" (METHODOLOGY §wall).\n- Neural embeddings were NOT available (no torch/sklearn/sentence-transformers); TF-IDF pure-Python keeps corpus-nav stdlib-pure and fast. True embeddings = a future dependency decision.\n\n## Open follow-ups\n- `find3` runs the 3 sources serially; `module_nav grep` is slow (~30–60s over 1046 files) → run the sources in parallel threads (proposed).\n- Optional: neural-embedding `semantic` backend behind a flag if a local model is ever installed.\n\n## Proposed kit deltas\n\n| # | Proposed change | Target (file · §/section) | Evidence | Type | Priority |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\nno new deltas; the kit already covers this run.\n"

Non-table content (prose, sub-headings only) under this heading\n> triggers a WARN — the reviewer must count by hand. **Exception:** a §18 honesty line\n> (`no new deltas; …`) placed here, or under `## Honest verdict`, is counted as a deliberate `~0`\n> — see §18 for accepted variants and location rules. Heading-style declarations **outside** this\n> section are non-conforming. Use the table below to stay machine-countable.\n>\n> **The heading text is matched literally — do not insert qualifier words.** Writing the kit's own\n> name between `Proposed` and `kit deltas` (e.g. `## Proposed research-sdd kit deltas`) or between\n> `Proposed` and `deltas` (e.g. `## Proposed research-sdd deltas`) breaks every recognised pattern\n> and makes this entire section invisible to supervision. The failure symptom visible to the author\n> is `empty-input: no delta section found` in `sweep-retros.sh` output — the delta table is\n> present and well-formed, yet the sweeper reports nothing. Use `## Proposed kit deltas` verbatim,\n> or an accepted alias listed in METHODOLOGY §18.\n\n## Already covered (dedupe — proof the retro read the kit first)\n\n> Lessons this run surfaced that the kit ALREADY encodes. Record every\n> tool here — \"we wrote a throwaway script\" IS a CREATED entry, not nothing; under-reporting is the\n> failure mode. Each column is answerable from the corpus and the run's commits alone.\n>\n> **ORACLE column** — an oracle is a tool that can **SEE** whether a result is correct rather than\n> **recompute** it: it observes from the viewer's or consumer's perspective (renders, displays, runs)\n> instead of repeating the same arithmetic path that produced the result. Example: a tool that renders\n> a 3D model exactly as the viewer will draw it can detect a mirror-flip that passes all 21\n> length/area/angle checks — because reflection preserves magnitudes, no symmetric check can see it.\n> Generic analysis tools belong in CREATED/ADAPTED, not ORACLE.
